text:
carmen: quick sync — hitting a weird routing mismatch. customer calls include X-Routing-Hint: dedicated-01 and a mobile User-Agent. Gateway routed to shared-host instead of dedicated pool. is precedence auth header -> routing hint -> ua-infer?

liam: i thought the rule was: if X-Routing-Hint present and signed allow override, else fallback to auth-based tenant routing, lastly ua inference. where did this deviate? can you paste a sample request?

carmen: paste from logs (redacted):
```
GET /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer redacted
User-Agent: RedwoodMobile/2.1 (Android)
X-Routing-Hint: dedicated-01
X-RW-Signature: null
```
Gateway decision log: matched route -> shared-host (reason: hint rejected, ua-score=0.7 matched shared pool)

srini: that's interesting — the code path currently does UA classification first to shortcut light requests, then applies header overrides only if sig present. bugs I've seen: signature check returns false on certain clients because we changed the key rotation window. so the header is treated as "present but invalid" and we ignore it.

maggie: confirmation: we intentionally built header overrides to be opt-in (whitelist + signed) to prevent spoofing. but we also added a safety rule: if auth tenant explicitly maps to dedicated pool, that should trump an untrusted header. maybe the auth->tenant mapping isn't set for this customer?

liam: can we add a small sanity rule: if X-Routing-Hint exists and auth indicates a tenant that *can* use that pool, prefer hint even if signature is missing, but emit a WARNING telemetry event? that would preserve customer intent for short term while we fix signature key rotation.

srini: not comfortable with unsigned acceptance. attacker could set header and escalate to expensive pool. safer path: fail open only for internal clients (whitelist) and emit metric. we need two things: 1) fix key rotation so signatures validate, 2) add telemetry counters and a dashboard so we can see how many requests are hitting signed vs unsigned hints.

carmen: agreed. for the immediate customer, we can add them to the header-whitelist (edge config) to unblock them. we should also update gateway ordering comment to be explicit. proposed precedence in words: "auth tenant mapping -> trusted header override -> user-agent inference -> fallback routing".

liam: sgtm. quick rollout plan:
- add customer to whitelist (edge config change) — canary to 10% internal region
- revert key-rotation bug (auth-keys service) — patch & deploy
- add telemetry counter: routing_hint.accepted, routing_hint.rejected(signature), routing_hint.unsigned_whitelisted
- dashboard tile in console (per-tenant) + alert if rejected/accepted rate > 0.1%

srini: i'll open a PR for the gateway ordering change and add unit tests for the signature window. also adding an e2e test case: header signed -> dedicated route chosen; header unsigned & not whitelisted -> not chosen.

maggie: deploy-bot: triggered canary for edge-config (whitelist add)
deploy-bot: Canary deployment started: edge-config v2026.3 -> regions: us-west-2 (10%). status: in-progress :rocket:

carmen: i'll create the RFC for the signed-header contract (fields: X-Routing-Hint, X-RW-Signature, X-RW-Timestamp) and link to the telemetry plan. also adding a small UX note for Console: show when route was overridden by header and whether it was trusted.

liam: thanks — one more ask: add a short note in the API docs about header semantics and security implications, and example for client SDK to sign hints.

srini: assigned: PR #2345 (gateway ordering), PR #2346 (auth-keys), ticket #789 (edge-whitelist), dashboard tile #456. I'll follow up with job to backfill metrics for last 72h so we can baseline.

carmen: perfect. tagging @maggie for customer comms. :eyes:

maggie: will draft a status note after canary success. :thumbsup:

liam: thanks all, looks like path forward.
